{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/paginator.py",
      "line": 182,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "BasePaginator now allows negative offsets that Django QuerySets cannot slice with",
      "body": "BasePaginator.get_result now uses cursor.offset directly when cursor.is_prev is true and then slices the queryset with that offset. Cursor strings can contain negative offsets, and this change permits them for previous pages. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indexing or negative offsets, so a client-supplied cursor such as 0:-1:1 can raise AssertionError or produce invalid SQL, causing 500s on any endpoint using this paginator."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/paginator.py",
      "line": 880,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "OptimizedCursorPaginator explicitly slices querysets with negative offsets",
      "body": "OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result sets start_offset to cursor.offset when enable_advanced_features is true and the offset is negative, then slices the Django queryset. Django does not support negative QuerySet indexing or slicing, so this will fail at runtime rather than provide efficient pagination. The audit-log endpoint enables this feature, so a negative cursor can crash the request. The negative offset is also left in later length checks, making result trimming unreliable."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py",
      "line": 79,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Optimized pagination is used with a datetime ordering field but only supports numeric keys",
      "body": "The endpoint selects OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by=-datetime. Unlike DateTimePaginator, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor or math.ceil on the field value, and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value instead of converting it to a datetime. With any non-empty audit-log page, get_item_key will receive a datetime and raise TypeError, and cursor values would not be converted correctly for the datetime filter. The optimized audit-log pagination path is therefore broken."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua",
      "line": 46,
      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Span buffer keys are changed from Redis sets to sorted sets without migration",
      "body": "The previous implementation stored span payloads in Redis sets using sadd, scard, sunionstore, and sscan. This change makes the Lua script and Python buffer operate on the same span-buf:s:* keys as sorted sets using zcard, zunionstore, zpopmin, zadd, and zscan. During deployment, in-flight keys created by the old code will still be sets, so new operations will fail with WRONGTYPE and span ingestion or flushing can break. A key namespace change, migration, or drain is needed."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua",
      "line": 47,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "ZUNIONSTORE uses the default SUM aggregation and can corrupt span scores",
      "body": "The sorted-set members are span payloads and their scores are end_timestamp_precise. ZUNIONSTORE is called without AGGREGATE MIN or MAX, so if a member exists in both source sets, for example due to duplicate messages or a span being present in both an old and merged buffer, Redis adds the two scores together. The resulting timestamp score is wrong, which can cause incorrect eviction ordering and make some spans never eligible for zpopmin."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua",
      "line": 63,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Segments over 1000 spans are silently truncated during insertion",
      "body": "When a merged span buffer has more than 1000 members, the script pops and discards the lowest-scored members. There is no metric, log, or tombstone indicating that spans were dropped, and the eviction can remove spans needed to assemble a complete segment, including potentially important root or parent spans. Flushed segments can therefore be incomplete without any observable signal. The limit is also hardcoded in Lua and ignores the Python max_segment_spans configuration."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua",
      "line": 30,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Redirect resolution limit lowered to 1000 can leave deep segment trees unjoined",
      "body": "The script follows at most 1000 redirect hops to find the canonical span buffer. If a redirect chain is longer than that, it stops early and stores the new span against an intermediate set instead of the final merged set. This can split a single trace segment into multiple buffers and produce incomplete or duplicated flushed segments. The previous limit was 10000, so this increases the correctness risk for deep or pathological traces."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py",
      "line": 73,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "No tests cover the new optimized audit-log pagination path",
      "body": "The endpoint adds a conditional OptimizedCursorPaginator path with advanced pagination behavior, but no API or paginator tests were added for it. The datetime incompatibility and negative-offset behavior introduced by this paginator are therefore unverified, and regressions in this privileged pagination path would not be caught."
    },
    {
      "file": "tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py",
      "line": 126,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "No tests cover the new sorted-set eviction or large-segment behavior",
      "body": "The PR introduces sorted-set storage, score-based eviction at 1000 spans, and a reduced redirect-depth limit, but the updated tests only add end_timestamp_precise to small fixtures. There is no test that inserts more than 1000 spans, verifies which spans are evicted, checks behavior when duplicate members are merged, or exercises redirect chains near the new limit."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: BasePaginator now allows negative offsets that Django QuerySets cannot slice with
findings.body: BasePaginator.get_result now uses cursor.offset directly when cursor.is_prev is true and then slices the queryset with that offset. Cursor strings can contain negative offsets, and this change permits them for previous pages. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indexing or negative offsets, so a client-supplied cursor such as 0:-1:1 can raise AssertionError or produce invalid SQL, causing 500s on any endpoint using this paginator.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator explicitly slices querysets with negative offsets
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result sets start_offset to cursor.offset when enable_advanced_features is true and the offset is negative, then slices the Django queryset. Django does not support negative QuerySet indexing or slicing, so this will fail at runtime rather than provide efficient pagination. The audit-log endpoint enables this feature, so a negative cursor can crash the request. The negative offset is also left in later length checks, making result trimming unreliable.

findings.title: Optimized pagination is used with a datetime ordering field but only supports numeric keys
findings.body: The endpoint selects OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by=-datetime. Unlike DateTimePaginator, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor or math.ceil on the field value, and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value instead of converting it to a datetime. With any non-empty audit-log page, get_item_key will receive a datetime and raise TypeError, and cursor values would not be converted correctly for the datetime filter. The optimized audit-log pagination path is therefore broken.

findings.title: Span buffer keys are changed from Redis sets to sorted sets without migration
findings.body: The previous implementation stored span payloads in Redis sets using sadd, scard, sunionstore, and sscan. This change makes the Lua script and Python buffer operate on the same span-buf:s:* keys as sorted sets using zcard, zunionstore, zpopmin, zadd, and zscan. During deployment, in-flight keys created by the old code will still be sets, so new operations will fail with WRONGTYPE and span ingestion or flushing can break. A key namespace change, migration, or drain is needed.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE uses the default SUM aggregation and can corrupt span scores
findings.body: The sorted-set members are span payloads and their scores are end_timestamp_precise. ZUNIONSTORE is called without AGGREGATE MIN or MAX, so if a member exists in both source sets, for example due to duplicate messages or a span being present in both an old and merged buffer, Redis adds the two scores together. The resulting timestamp score is wrong, which can cause incorrect eviction ordering and make some spans never eligible for zpopmin.

findings.title: Segments over 1000 spans are silently truncated during insertion
findings.body: When a merged span buffer has more than 1000 members, the script pops and discards the lowest-scored members. There is no metric, log, or tombstone indicating that spans were dropped, and the eviction can remove spans needed to assemble a complete segment, including potentially important root or parent spans. Flushed segments can therefore be incomplete without any observable signal. The limit is also hardcoded in Lua and ignores the Python max_segment_spans configuration.

findings.title: Redirect resolution limit lowered to 1000 can leave deep segment trees unjoined
findings.body: The script follows at most 1000 redirect hops to find the canonical span buffer. If a redirect chain is longer than that, it stops early and stores the new span against an intermediate set instead of the final merged set. This can split a single trace segment into multiple buffers and produce incomplete or duplicated flushed segments. The previous limit was 10000, so this increases the correctness risk for deep or pathological traces.

findings.title: No tests cover the new optimized audit-log pagination path
findings.body: The endpoint adds a conditional OptimizedCursorPaginator path with advanced pagination behavior, but no API or paginator tests were added for it. The datetime incompatibility and negative-offset behavior introduced by this paginator are therefore unverified, and regressions in this privileged pagination path would not be caught.

findings.title: No tests cover the new sorted-set eviction or large-segment behavior
findings.body: The PR introduces sorted-set storage, score-based eviction at 1000 spans, and a reduced redirect-depth limit, but the updated tests only add end_timestamp_precise to small fixtures. There is no test that inserts more than 1000 spans, verifies which spans are evicted, checks behavior when duplicate members are merged, or exercises redirect chains near the new limit.
